<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

<!-- PR title: [Type] scope: title, or [Type] [Hardware] scope: title.
Type: Feat, Fix, Refactor, Perf, Doc, Test, CI, or Chore.
Scope: any module or model name (no fixed list or letter-case restriction), e.g. attention, qwen3, or flash-attn.
Hardware: optional single tag without spaces. Use uppercase hardware tags (AMD, NVIDIA, NPU, MI300X), except for exactly these four spellings: Intel, Apple, Huawei, Ascend.
Title: no letter-case restriction.
Reverts: use GitHub's default title, Revert "original title".
Examples: [Fix] attention: Fix KV cache indexing; [Perf] [AMD] flash-attn: Optimize decode performance. -->

## Motivation

The NPU precision-test (coverage-based test selection) pipeline consumes a prebuilt
baseline: `test_case_map.json` (test case → covered lines) plus `outputs.tar.gz`
(the `covstub` source tree). Both files were expected in OBS, but they had to be
uploaded **manually** after each `Coverage Collection (NPU)` run. A forgotten
upload meant `recommend-tests-from-coverage` silently fell back to a stale
baseline, and the mis-selection was invisible until a regression slipped through.

The baseline also had no quality floor: a run whose coverage collapsed (missing
subprocess data, skipped suites, partial job failures) would happily overwrite a
good baseline, degrading every subsequent PR's test selection with no signal.

At the same time, the new automated upload must not become a single point of
failure — the shared-disk baseline is still the primary artifact, and readers of
that disk must not lose it just because an external bucket was unreachable.

<!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. -->

## Modifications

Workflow-only changes in `.github/workflows/pr-test-npu.yml`; product code and
test behavior are untouched. Everything below runs only in
`coverage_mode: true` (the `setup-covstub` job), i.e. never on a normal PR run.

- **Single source of truth for the NPU-only coverage number.** The
  `Generate HTML coverage report` step now computes the NPU-only total once,
  writes it to `${RUN_DIR}/npu_coverage.txt`, and the run-page summary reuses
  that same value. The number shown to reviewers and the number gated on can
  no longer diverge; the file is written unconditionally because
  `GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` may be unset on the k8s runner pool.

- **New `Upload baseline to OBS` step.** Replaces the manual push:
  - Skips (warning only) when `test_case_map.json` / `outputs.tar.gz` are
    missing, so an empty run can never overwrite a good baseline.
  - Fails closed if `npu_coverage.txt` is absent (e.g. the report step died
    before writing it).
  - Enforces an `MIN_NPU_COVERAGE=40` floor on NPU-only line coverage; below
    it the upload is rejected instead of poisoning the baseline.
  - Skips (warning only) when `OBS_ACCESS_KEY_PRECISION` /
    `OBS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY_PRECISION` are not configured.
  - Bootstraps `obsutil` on demand, uploads with `-acl=public-read`, then
    verifies each object with an anonymous HTTPS `HEAD` == 200 — a stale
    private ACL would otherwise only surface as a confusing failure in the
    next run's download step.

- **`Publish outputs and map to shared disk` is now `if: ${{ !cancelled() }}`.**
  A failed OBS upload no longer skips the primary shared-disk publish.

- **`Clean up per-run directory` keeps default `success()` and also sweeps
  residue.** Any earlier failure (including the OBS upload) still preserves
  `RUN_DIR` for manual recovery; on success it additionally deletes
  `*-attempt-*` directories older than 8h, at `-maxdepth 1` so the shared
  `coverage/` dir and concurrently running jobs are never touched.

<!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. -->

## Accuracy Tests

<!-- If this pull request affects model outputs (e.g., changes to the kernel or model forward code), provide accuracy test results. -->

## Speed Tests and Profiling

<!-- If this pull request impacts inference speed, provide benchmarking and profiling results. -->

## Checklist

- [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

files.patch:
@@ -1032,8 +1032,18 @@ jobs:
             --include='*/sglang/srt/hardware_backend/npu/*' \
             --directory="${REPORT_DIR}-npu"
 
+          # Compute the NPU-only TOTAL once: it feeds both the run-page summary
+          # and the OBS coverage gate (${RUN_DIR}/npu_coverage.txt), so the
+          # gated number and the displayed number cannot diverge. Written
+          # unconditionally because GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY may be unset on the
+          # k8s runner pool while the gate still needs the value.
+          NPU_TOTAL_LINE="$(COVERAGE_FILE=/tmp/.coverage-npu \
+            python3 -m coverage report --rcfile=/tmp/report-rc \
+            --include='*/sglang/srt/hardware_backend/npu/*' | tail -n 1)"
+          printf '%s\n' "${NPU_TOTAL_LINE}" | awk '{print $NF}' | tr -d '%' \
+            > "${RUN_DIR}/npu_coverage.txt"
+
           # Surface the totals directly on the run page.
-          # GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY may be unset on the k8s runner pool.
           if [ -n "${GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY:-}" ]; then
             {
               echo "### Coverage"
@@ -1042,9 +1052,7 @@ jobs:
               COVERAGE_FILE=/tmp/.coverage-all \
                 python3 -m coverage report --rcfile=/tmp/report-rc | tail -n 1
               echo "python/sglang/srt/hardware_backend/npu (full-tree denominator):"
-              COVERAGE_FILE=/tmp/.coverage-npu \
-                python3 -m coverage report --rcfile=/tmp/report-rc \
-                --include='*/sglang/srt/hardware_backend/npu/*' | tail -n 1
+              echo "${NPU_TOTAL_LINE}"
               echo '```'
               echo "Full line-by-line report: download the \`coverage-html-report\` artifact and open \`htmlcov/index.html\` (NPU-only view: \`htmlcov-npu/index.html\`)."
             } >> "${GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY}"
@@ -1113,16 +1121,107 @@ jobs:
           if-no-files-found: ignore
           retention-days: 14
 
+      - name: Upload baseline to OBS
+        shell: bash
+        env:
+          # Ascend repo's OBS writer credentials (precision baseline bucket).
+          OBS_ACCESS_KEY_ID: ${{ secrets.OBS_ACCESS_KEY_PRECISION }}
+          OBS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY: ${{ secrets.OBS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY_PRECISION }}
+        run: |
+          set -euo pipefail
+
+          RUN_DIR="/root/.cache/tests/precise-test/${{ github.run_id }}-attempt-${{ github.run_attempt }}"
+          OBS_ENDPOINT="${OBS_ENDPOINT:-obs.cn-southwest-2.myhuaweicloud.com}"
+          OBS_BUCKET="${OBS_BUCKET:-sglang-npu}"
+          # TEMP: debug prefix, revert to "coverage" once verified.
+          OBS_PREFIX="${OBS_PREFIX:-coverage/pr}"
+
+          # Same skip rule as publish: no map -> incomplete baseline, never
+          # overwrite the good one in OBS.
+          if [ ! -s "${RUN_DIR}/test_case_map.json" ] || [ ! -s "${RUN_DIR}/outputs.tar.gz" ]; then
+            echo "::warning::test_case_map.json or outputs.tar.gz missing (no coverage data this run), skip OBS upload"
+            exit 0
+          fi
+
+          # NPU-only coverage gate: only the threshold comparison lives here.
+          # The percentage is computed once by the "Generate HTML coverage
+          # report" step above (same container). Fail closed when the value is
+          # missing, e.g. that step died before writing it.
+          MIN_NPU_COVERAGE=40
+          NPU_PCT_FILE="${RUN_DIR}/npu_coverage.txt"
+          if [ ! -s "${NPU_PCT_FILE}" ]; then
+            echo "::error::NPU-only coverage value missing (${NPU_PCT_FILE}); refusing to upload the baseline to OBS"
+            exit 1
+          fi
+          NPU_PCT="$(<"${NPU_PCT_FILE}")"
+          echo "NPU-only coverage: ${NPU_PCT}% (threshold: ${MIN_NPU_COVERAGE}%)"
+          if ! awk "BEGIN {exit !(${NPU_PCT} >= ${MIN_NPU_COVERAGE})}"; then
+            echo "::error::NPU-only coverage ${NPU_PCT}% is below ${MIN_NPU_COVERAGE}%, skip OBS upload"
+            exit 1
+          fi
+
+          if [ -z "${OBS_ACCESS_KEY_ID:-}" ] || [ -z "${OBS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY:-}" ]; then
+            echo "::warning::OBS_ACCESS_KEY_PRECISION/OBS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY_PRECISION secrets not set, skip OBS upload"
+            exit 0
+          fi
+
+          if ! command -v obsutil >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+            curl -fsSL \
+              --retry 3 \
+              --retry-delay 5 \
+              --retry-all-errors \
+              "https://obs-community.obs.cn-north-1.myhuaweicloud.com/obsutil/current/obsutil_linux_amd64.tar.gz" \
+              -o /tmp/obsutil.tar.gz
+            tar xzf /tmp/obsutil.tar.gz -C /tmp
+            OBSUTIL="$(find /tmp -maxdepth 2 -path '/tmp/obsutil_linux_amd64_*/obsutil' -type f -print -quit)"
+            chmod +x "${OBSUTIL}"
+            install -m 0755 "${OBSUTIL}" /usr/local/bin/obsutil 2>/dev/null \
+              || { mkdir -p /tmp/bin && cp "${OBSUTIL}" /tmp/bin/obsutil && export PATH="/tmp/bin:${PATH}"; }
+          fi
+
+          obsutil config \
+            -i="${OBS_ACCESS_KEY_ID}" \
+            -k="${OBS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY}" \
+            -e="${OBS_ENDPOINT}"
+
+          # ACL lives on the object, not on the key: overwriting uploads a new
+          # object that inherits the bucket default (private), while the
+          # recommend job fetches these over anonymous HTTPS. Pass ACL in the
+          # upload request itself so an interruption cannot leave behind an
+          # object that exists but is private.
+          for f in outputs.tar.gz test_case_map.json; do
+            obj="obs://${OBS_BUCKET}/${OBS_PREFIX}/${f}"
+            obsutil cp "${RUN_DIR}/${f}" "${obj}" -f -acl=public-read
+          done
+
+          # Anonymous-read check: a stale private ACL here would only surface
+          # as a confusing failure in the next run's download steps.
+          for f in outputs.tar.gz test_case_map.json; do
+            code="$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' -I -L \
+              "https://${OBS_BUCKET}.${OBS_ENDPOINT}/${OBS_PREFIX}/${f}")"
+            echo "${f}: anonymous HEAD -> HTTP ${code}"
+            if [ "${code}" != "200" ]; then
+              echo "::error::${f} not publicly readable (HTTP ${code}); check its ACL"
+              exit 1
+            fi
+          done
+
+          echo "Uploaded baseline to obs://${OBS_BUCKET}/${OBS_PREFIX}/"
+          ls -lh "${RUN_DIR}/outputs.tar.gz" "${RUN_DIR}/test_case_map.json"
+
       - name: Publish outputs and map to shared disk
+        # Runs even if the OBS upload above failed: the shared-disk baseline is
+        # the primary product, the OBS copy is only for the recommend job.
+        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
         shell: bash
         run: |
           set -euo pipefail
 
           RUN_DIR="/root/.cache/tests/precise-test/${{ github.run_id }}-attempt-${{ github.run_attempt }}"
           # Fixed-name copy for manual use; the recommend job's baseline lives
-          # in OBS (upload outputs.tar.gz + test_case_map.json manually after
-          # each run). coverage-data.tar.gz has no automatic consumer — no OBS
-          # copy, only this dir and the precise-test-coverage-data artifact.
+          # in OBS, refreshed by the "Upload baseline to OBS" step above.
+          # coverage-data.tar.gz has no automatic consumer — no OBS copy, only
+          # this dir and the precise-test-coverage-data artifact.
           PUBLISH_DIR="/root/.cache/tests/precise-test/coverage"
 
           # Skip publish when no coverage data this run — never overwrite
@@ -1159,13 +1258,26 @@ jobs:
           ls -lh "${PUBLISH_DIR}" | tail -n +2
 
       - name: Clean up per-run directory
-        # Skipped on publish failure, keeping RUN_DIR for manual recovery.
+        # Default success() on purpose: any earlier failure (incl. the OBS
+        # upload) keeps RUN_DIR for manual recovery.
+        # A successful run also sweeps leftovers from earlier failed runs, so
+        # residue does not pile up. Only dirs older than STALE_MINUTES: RUN_DIR
+        # is per-run for a reason, and a bare glob would delete the directory
+        # of a concurrently running job mid-flight.
         shell: bash
         run: |
           set -euo pipefail
-          RUN_DIR="/root/.cache/tests/precise-test/${{ github.run_id }}-attempt-${{ github.run_attempt }}"
+          CACHE_ROOT="/root/.cache/tests/precise-test"
+          RUN_DIR="${CACHE_ROOT}/${{ github.run_id }}-attempt-${{ github.run_attempt }}"
+          # 8h > the 6h per-job execution limit, so a live run can never match.
+          STALE_MINUTES=480
           rm -rf "${RUN_DIR}"
           echo "Removed ${RUN_DIR}"
+          # -maxdepth 1 keeps the shared coverage/ dir out of reach.
+          find "${CACHE_ROOT}" -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 -type d \
+            -name '*-attempt-*' -mmin +"${STALE_MINUTES}" \
+            -print -exec rm -rf {} +
+          echo "Swept stale run dirs older than ${STALE_MINUTES}min"
 
   pr-test-npu-finish:
     needs:
